title: Precision leash and grace-period autoscale regulator
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem statement: Dedicated fleets must provide predictable throughput guarantees while avoiding oscillation, wasted cost, and cold-start latency for tenant traffic. Existing single-signal scalers (latency-only or token-rate-only) either over-provision during bursts or under-react to sudden demand shifts. Goal: design and ship a policy engine component — the Precision Leash & Grace-Period Autoscale Regulator — that composes multiple target metrics, supports hybrid scaling algorithms (predictive + reactive), and enforces safety limits (slew, min/max capacity, rollback windows) to deliver stable, cost-conscious scaling for Dedicated pools.

Design summary: The regulator evaluates a prioritized metric set per-tenant and per-fleet: token_throughput (tokens/sec), request_throughput (req/sec), p95_latency, queue_depth, and warm_fraction (percent of warm inference workers). Each metric has a configurable target and weight. A scoring function produces a blended scale intent which is fed into a two-stage algorithm: 1) predictive warmup predictor (short-term demand forecasting using lightweight exponential smoothing with traffic-aware seasonality) that suggests pre-warm capacity, and 2) constrained stepper which applies hard safety envelopes (max_delta_per_minute, min_capacity, max_capacity) and stochastic dampening (variance-aware backoff) before emitting a capacity change.

Scaling algorithms and rules:
- Metric composition: metrics -> normalized ratio to target -> weighted max/sum fusion with fallbacks.
- Predictive layer: EWMA with multiple horizons (30s, 2m, 10m) and a traffic classification feature (steady / spiky / batch) to bias forecasts.
- Reactive layer: derivative-based detector for sudden ramps (detect slope > threshold) that triggers guarded step increases with a short-lived surge window.
- Safety envelopes: min_capacity (per-tenant floor), max_capacity (global or SKU-bound), slew_rate_limit (percentage-of-current-per-minute), cooldown windows (grace period after scale-up/down), and rollback triggers (error-rate or p95 breach after scale event).
- Cost-aware tie-breaker: when multiple scale candidates are equal, prefer options minimizing expected token-cost (model variant and quantization preferences consulted).

Safety limits and guardrails:
- Default slew_limit: 30% capacity increase per minute (configurable).
- Cooldown windows: 90s after scale-up, 120s after scale-down before further increases/decreases are allowed (except critical emergency responses).
- Rollback conditions: if p95 latency increases by >30% or error-rate rises >2x within 3 minutes of a scale event, automatically revert last scale action and mark incident for investigation.
- KV-affinity preservation: avoid scaling decisions that would evict >X% of tenants with pinned KV cache; prefer adding nodes over removing if eviction cost would be high.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressiveness vs cost: tighter targets reduce latency but increase committed spend. We provide per-tenant QoS tiers (economy, standard, premium) to map default weights and safety profiles.
- Complexity vs predictability: forecasting improves headroom but can mispredict rare traffic shapes; forecasting weight is tunable and off by default for tenants with <1 req/s average.

Implementation plan (phased):
1) PoC: implement metric fusion and constrained stepper simulator (local), evaluate on historical traces for 6 weeks.
2) Canary 1: deploy regulator in read-only mode (suggestions surfaced in console) for selected internal teams; compare recommendations to current controller.
3) Canary 2: enable automated scale-ups only with manual approval for scale-downs for 10% of fleets.
4) Gradual rollout: enable both directions + predictive warmup for Premium pools; monitor for 4 weeks before wider enablement.

Testing strategy:
- Offline replay tests using 12 months of production traces, synthetic spike campaigns, and adversarial sequences to verify stability and bounds.
- Chaos tests: force partial fleet outages and KV eviction scenarios to validate rollback and affinity heuristics.
- Canary telemetry: compare p50/p95 token latency, cost per 1M tokens, and SLA miss rate relative to baseline.

Acceptance criteria:
- No increase in SLA miss rate for canary fleets during a 2-week window (<0.1% regression).
- Reduction in cold-start tail latency (p99 cold-start) by >= 20% for premium tenants after predictive warmup enabled.
- Cost delta: dedicated spend change <= +5% for premium canaries while achieving latency targets.
- Automated rollout must include transparent audit logs and ability to revert within 10 minutes.

Observability and dashboarding:
- New console panels per-fleet: scale intent history, metric contributions (per-metric score), active safety constraints, and recently executed rollbacks.
- Alerting: escalations for frequent rollbacks (>3 in 1 hour), repeated oscillation patterns, or predictive model drift (forecast vs observed error >25% over 1h).

Backward compatibility and migration:
- Controller runs alongside existing autoscaler with a shadow mode for 2 weeks. All regulator decisions are emitted to event log and traceable by trace-id.
- Tenants can opt-out to legacy controller via fleet annotation; defaults vary by QoS tier.

Risks and mitigations:
- Forecasting misfires: mitigate by conservative default forecast weight and automated disable if drift detected.
- Eviction storms: KV-affinity heuristics to avoid mass evictions; prefer throttled downsizes.
- Complexity in config surface: expose sensible presets and a concise ‘safety profile’ API for common cases.

Rollout checklist:
- [x] Simulator validated on replay: perf/regressions.json attached to ticket.
- [x] Design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QpPrecisionLeashDesign (internal)
- [ ] PR: infra change and operator UI (work in progress) https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1287
- [ ] Canary deployment runbook and rollback playbook (draft).

Notes: This ticket covers the policy engine logic and operator controls. Separate tickets will implement full console UX, per-tenant policy API, and long-term ML-based forecaster replacement.
